topic: Data Alignment and Memory Access Optimization
explanation: Data alignment refers to the placement of data objects in memory such that their addresses are multiples of their size.  This is crucial for performance optimization because it simplifies memory access.  Unaligned data can require multiple memory accesses to retrieve a single object, slowing down program execution.  Alignment improves efficiency by allowing the processor to fetch data in a single operation, thus reducing memory access time and improving overall system performance.
